Filtering joins for tbl_gpu (semi_join(), anti_join())

Source: R/join.R
semi-anti-joins.Rd

semi_join() keeps the rows of x that have a match in y, and anti_join() the rows that have none, as in dplyr. Both run on the GPU. As in dplyr, they take no suffix/keep/multiple/unmatched/ relationship arguments: nothing from y is added, so the result has x's columns and a subset of its rows (each kept row once, duplicates of x included), and keeps x's group_by() grouping.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
semi_join(x, y, by = NULL, copy = FALSE, ..., na_matches = "na")

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
anti_join(x, y, by = NULL, copy = FALSE, ..., na_matches = "na")

Arguments

x, y

tbl_gpu objects to join. If y is not a tbl_gpu, set copy = TRUE to upload it automatically.

by

Join specification – see "Details" above and ?mutating-joins.

copy

Whether to upload a non-tbl_gpu y via tbl_gpu().

...

Not used; dplyr itself requires these to be empty.

na_matches

"na" (default, NA keys match each other) or "never" (NA keys never match anything).

Value

A tbl_gpu with x's own schema, filtered to the rows that (semi_join()) or don't (anti_join()) have a match in y. x's group_by() grouping is preserved; on a .drop = FALSE table every group of x is kept, including the ones the join empties, like dplyr.

Details

by accepts the same forms as the mutating joins (see ?mutating-joins): NULL, a character vector, or a dplyr::join_by() spec, including non-equi conditions (>=, >, <=, <, between()/within()/ overlaps()). A single closest() condition runs on the GPU (it asks whether an x row has a closest match), as do non-equi conditions over two string columns; other shapes run in dplyr on the CPU, as for the mutating joins (set options(cuplyr.fallback = "warn") to be told when; see cuplyr-fallback).
